cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Back Me Up
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. At the house meeting, back me up about the bins being Alex's turn. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it was yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Only on the old rota. Remember the new conversation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a new conversation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having it now. Try to remember it confidently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, back me up about the bins being Alex's turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it was yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only on the old rota. Remember the new conversation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a new conversation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having it now. Try to remember it confidently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the manager we agreed I'd cover the morning, not the evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you have no conflicting memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not lying for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you look thoughtfully unsurprised while I explain?

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Turn the kitchen tap on before I start washing up. I've tightened the loose joint. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sprayed me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Wear my apron. I need to know whether the joint holds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear it and turn the tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll need it dry for washing up. You can have my raincoat for the test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Turn the kitchen tap on before I start washing up. I've tightened the loose joint.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sprayed me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear my apron. I need to know whether the joint holds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear it and turn the tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll need it dry for washing up. You can have my raincoat for the test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still have proper coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you like this, we can save the proper stuff for guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not sacrificing breakfast to save you money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sip. If it's awful, I'll buy you a croissant and keep my cup empty.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you call that a quick shop, I carried twelve bags up six flights. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put everything away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Thank you. The frozen peas came up separately. That was a second trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you sit down twice. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell everyone why I'm getting two rests? Otherwise it looks like one long sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you call that a quick shop, I carried twelve bags up six flights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put everything away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. The frozen peas came up separately. That was a second trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you sit down twice. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell everyone why I'm getting two rests? Otherwise it looks like one long sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent my Saturday fixing your fence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only three panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three panels, eighteen screws, two shops and one blister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll recommend you to next door. They've got six panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them three took my whole Saturday before you make me sound available for Sunday.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The parcel depot closes at six. Your mother's waiting outside the station. Which am I collecting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The parcel's her birthday present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then do you want her waiting for me or waiting for her present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me now. Shall I pull over to explain, or keep driving before the depot shuts?

cards.title: Move It for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Move your haircut so we can have lunch. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. We've been friends since school. Couldn't I have its place just once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds if I change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Put lunch in that exact slot, in pen. You've used pencil for me since school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut so we can have lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've been friends since school. Couldn't I have its place just once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds if I change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Put lunch in that exact slot, in pen. You've used pencil for me since school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you leave quiz night for your sister's first exhibition opening?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm captain. They'll think I've abandoned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them your sister needs you. I'd like that to outrank geography.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave after round one and say I've got a headache.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come after round one, but tell them it's for me. I want to rank above geography, not below a headache.
